title: This text discusses the legal concepts of duress, undue influence, and utmost good faith in contracts. Duress refers to situations where a person is forced to act against their will, while undue influence involves subtle pressure that leads someone to make decisions they wouldn't normally make, often seen in relationships like parent-child or doctor-patient. The text cites notable legal cases to illustrate these concepts, emphasizing the importance of independent advice in financial decisions. Additionally, it touches on the moral implications of these concepts in a religious context, stating that individuals cannot use external influences as excuses for their sins and must take responsibility for their actions to attain spiritual redemption.
